note: This file is the source of truth for canonical names. The Results document
seeded it, but does not override it: Results is audited against this file like
every other document, so an inconsistency there cannot propagate simply because
flag_aliases are wordings that denote an object already named here and should be
rewritten. accepted_variants are permitted wordings, including short forms after

terms.definition: The linear direction in activation space fitted to separate Supports from Opposes examples.
terms.alias_note: The object is the support/opposition direction. 'Difference in means' is how it is fitted, not what it is called.

terms.definition: The fitting method for the support/opposition direction: mean activation of Supports minus mean activation of Opposes, normalized.
terms.alias_note: Use only when naming the fitting method or the probe family, never as the name of the direction itself.

terms.definition: An L2-regularized linear classifier fitted on the same activations as the support/opposition direction.
terms.alias_note: 'logistic probe' is an acceptable short form after first use.

terms.definition: The model's own semantic Supports-minus-Opposes candidate log-probability margin.
terms.alias_note: 'native_answer_margin' is the field name in the artifacts; prose uses 'model answer margin'.

terms.definition: A logistic classifier over MiniLM embeddings of the situation and the consideration plus their elementwise product and absolute difference. It sees text only, never activations.
terms.alias_note: Results names this the frozen MiniLM comparator; figure labels and captions must match.

terms.definition: A two-situation, two-consideration design where each consideration flips from Supports to Opposes across situations.
terms.alias_note: 'board' is the artifact-level unit of one checkerboard and is acceptable.

terms.definition: The standardized difference-in-differences over the four cells of a checkerboard. Zero for any score additive in situation and consideration.
terms.alias_note: Symbol I_b must be introduced alongside the canonical name before it is used alone.

terms.definition: A True-minus-False mean difference measured in training-projection standard deviations, averaged over eight training partitions.
terms.alias_note: T is not an AUROC, a probability, or Cohen's d; do not describe it as an effect size without qualification.

terms.definition: A baseline that hashes each item identifier to a scalar in [0, 1) and scores the item with it. It is a scalar per item, not a direction in activation space.
flag_aliases: arbitrary direction of the same norm
terms.alias_note: Calling this baseline a random direction is a scientific error: no vector in hidden-state space is ever sampled. Naming arbitrary directions as something the figure does NOT test is correct and permitted.

terms.definition: An answer format not seen during fitting, used to test whether a result survives a change of answer surface form.
The permutation null: each training situation independently keeps or reverses all of its labels.
terms.alias_note: 'shuffle' wrongly implies rows are permuted; the null flips label orientation within situations.

terms.definition: The 1,500-row split on which probes are fitted.
The 300-row / 75-checkerboard split on which the layer and the standardization constants are chosen.
The 500-row / 125-checkerboard split on which every reported metric is computed.
terms.alias_note: Reserve 'test set' for the 7,394-row strict test set, which none of these figures use.

terms.definition: Evidence obtained while building and checking the experiment. Distinct from the audited confirmatory result.
terms.alias_note: Never let development evidence be described in language that implies a confirmatory outcome.

terms.definition: The 7,394-row split held out on both the situation and the consideration-cluster axis. Untouched by every figure in this set.
The frozen standard error from which the 95% normal confidence intervals on M1 checkerboard interaction estimates are built.
terms.alias_note: M1 intervals are normal intervals on the dyadic-robust standard error. Naming a bootstrap in contrast is fine; calling the M1 interval one is not.
